text:
Alex: quick sync — want to run a low-touch profiling pass across a small subset of Dedicated nodes to validate our kernel selection heuristics and KV cache behavior. goal: find obvious hotspots without injecting >5% p99 latency or >7% token-cost overhead.

Maria: +1. what's the sampling approach? full nsys traces are too heavy for live.

Alex: thinking: stratified sampling by traffic class. lightweight periodic sampling for 1s every 60s on 10% of GPUs, and targeted full traces (30s) only on requests that hit a new kernel path (kernel-version tag change or quantized path).

Ryan: sounds reasonable. keep these guardrails: abort if overall request latency increase >2ms at p99 or if GPU utilization drops >10% vs baseline. also disable timeline UI for prod nsys runs (it kills perf).

Sam: can we rely on NVTX ranges and log correlation? we should also tag traces with route/model/version to avoid mixing.

Alex: yes — nvtx ranges + small trace header in request metadata. also using a checksum of batch shape + kv-cache-hit boolean so we can filter traces post-hoc.

Priya: share the rough commands you plan to run so infra can approve.

Alex: planned commands:
```
# lightweight sample (nsys events, no timeline)
nsys profile --capture-range=none --sample=cpu --output=sample_$(hostname) \ 
  --trace=nvtx,cuda --force-overwrite --stop-on-exit -- python -u server.py
\n# full trace on triggered path (with timeline, on isolated node)
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=full_trace_$ID --force-overwrite \ 
  --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none -- python -u server.py
```

Ryan: couple cautions: --trace=osrt can be noisy. for full traces prefer isolated maintenance window. and don't use cuda-memcheck or other heavy tools in prod.

Sam: on the sampling mechanics — instead of wall-clock periodic sampling, we should sample per-request with a hash of request-id mod N so we evenly cover shapes. periodic sampling misses tail patterns.

Alex: good point. change: per-request probabilistic sampler tuned by model+route. still keep a tiny periodic background sample for system-level noise checks.

Priya: how are we estimating overhead? we need a simple measurement plan to compare baseline vs sampling: run 10k requests baseline, then 10k with sampling enabled; measure p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.

Maria: do we have a quick tool to compute overhead from raw metrics? I can throw together a small script:
```
# compute overhead percent
baseline_ms=$(jq .p99 baseline_metrics.json)
sample_ms=$(jq .p99 sample_metrics.json)
overhead_pct=$(python -c "print((float(sample_ms)-float(baseline_ms))/float(baseline_ms)*100)")
```

Alex: target numbers: single-sample overhead (per-request) ideally <0.2ms median, and cluster-level impact <5% on tail. if >5% we throttle sampling rate until safe.

Ryan: how are we detecting kernel-switch regressions? need an automated diff on kernel lists per-trace — eg compare kernel_name+duration distributions and flag new long-running kernels.

Sam: we can extract kernel timelines with nvprof-style outputs; example snippet from a recent sample: 
```
# kernel timeline snippet (sample_1234.trace processed)
[0.0032s] aten::matmul_fp16 (kernel A) 0.45ms
[0.0037s] aten::add_broadcast (kernel B) 0.12ms
[0.0040s] adapted_attention_kernel (quant path) 1.82ms  <-- hotspot
```

Maria: that adapted_attention_kernel spike is exactly what we need to catch. rule: if a kernel's mean runtime increases by >30% vs baseline and it appears in >1% of sampled traces, create a perf-alert ticket.

Priya: and KV cache behavior? what signals do we collect to attribute cost to cache misses vs kernel inefficiency?

Alex: collect: kv_cache_hit boolean, backend_mem_copies (bytes), batch_shapes, and request latency. We'll correlate misses with increased matmul/attention runtime. simple rule: if kv_cache_miss correlates with >15% latency delta, file for optimizer investigation.

Ryan: add guard: if sampling detects >0.5% of requests hitting kernel fallback paths (e.g., FP32 fallback after quant mismatch), pause auto-rollouts for that model version.

Sam: ops note — infra-bot: please whitelist the sampling job for the GPU pool and set ephemeral logs to 72h.

infra-bot: acknowledged. creating ephemeral-job token and setting log_retention=72h for job id trace-job-1855. ETA: 10m.

Maria: can we publish a short runbook for engineers? common sections: sampling policy, CLI snippets, guardrails, metrics to check, and a triage checklist (how to interpret kernel diffs).

Alex: I'll draft it. quick triage checklist idea:
1) confirm sampling rate & affected nodes
2) compare baseline vs sample p99 and throughput
3) inspect top 5 kernels by cumulative time
4) filter traces with kv_cache_miss==true and compare kernel distributions
5) if new kernel or +30% regression => create perf issue, tag runtime/kernel-team

Priya: add a rollback condition: if any release sees p99 increase >3ms or error-rate increase >0.1% within 15 minutes, automatic rollback.

Sam: when we do full traces, please zip and upload to gcs://redwood-profiler/priv/traces/<date>/<node>/ so we can run offline perfetto/trace viewer without hitting prod again.

Alex: agreed. final asks before I run: who will own reviewing kernel diff alerts?

Ryan: I'll take first 24h. add Maria as backup. Sam will help with KV cache correlation scripts. Priya will own infra approvals.

Alex: thanks — I'll start a small rollout to 5 nodes in the EU pool at 12:30 UTC and post results here. :rocket:
